extracted.intended_audience: FCC staff, agency debt-collection officers, legal practitioners handling FCC-related debt collection
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements (47 CFR Part 1 subpart) that govern how the FCC identifies, demands, offsets, compromises, and collects debts (including salary offsets and contracts with private collectors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to law and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall implement the requirements of applicable law and government-wide standards (e.g., 31 U.S.C. 3701-3719, 5 CFR part 550, 31 CFR parts 900-904) and where circumstances are not covered by these regulations the Commission will proceed in accordance with applicable requirements found in the referenced standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every item in the referenced standards has been incorporated; where gaps exist the Commission will follow the applicable government-wide standards referenced in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other procedures; collection of forfeiture penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations do not require the Commission to duplicate contractually- or statutorily-required administrative or other proceedings, and do not supersede procedures permitted or required by other statutes or regulations (e.g., assessment and collection of monetary forfeitures initially governed by 47 U.S.C. 503, 504 and 47 CFR 1.80).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After compliance with statutory procedures, the Commission may use collection alternatives in this subpart; nothing restricts other rights to recover amounts owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of informal administrative actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in these regulations precludes utilization of informal administrative actions or remedies (including Alternative Dispute Resolution) or exercising rights agreed to among the parties in written agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal remedies remain available and may be used in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of property or collateral
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may demand return of specific property or, as a non-exclusive alternative, require return of property or payment of its value or the amount due under any agreement or Commission rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not limit other rights under law, regulation, or agreement; Commission acts as regulator under the Communications Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omissions by the Commission not a defense
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure or omission of the Commission to comply with any provision in this regulation shall not serve as a defense to any debtor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A debtor cannot rely on Commission procedural omissions as a defense to liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of applications for unpaid fees, delinquent debts, or debarment
rubrics_metrics.description: An application subject to the FCC Registration Number (FRN) requirement will be examined to determine if the applicant has paid appropriate application or regulatory fees, is delinquent in debts owed the Commission, or is debarred from receiving Federal benefits; fee/delinquency checks are examined based on the entity's taxpayer identifying number (TIN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 47 CFR 1.8002(b)(1) for TIN use and 47 CFR part 1, subpart G for handling entities that have not paid proper fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of applications by delinquent entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Action will be withheld on applications or requests for authorization by any entity found to be delinquent in its debt to the Commission unless otherwise provided; the entity will be informed that action is withheld until full payment or arrangement to pay is made and the application may be dismissed if not remedied within 30 days of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any Commission action taken prior to payment is contingent and subject to rescission; failure to pay may subject debtor to collection including interest, penalties, and collection costs under 31 U.S.C. 3717.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions for emergency authorizations and bankruptcy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for emergency or special temporary authority involving safety of life or property or brief transition periods will not be subject to the withholding provisions; the withholding provisions also do not apply where 11 U.S.C. 525(a) is applicable or where the applicant timely files an administrative appeal or judicial challenge to the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The withholding rules apply to permanent authorizations for these services; bankruptcy filings generally halt collection activity until legal advice is obtained and the automatic stay is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand for payment: general requirement and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Written demand (letter, order, memorandum, or other form) will be made promptly to inform the debtor of consequences of failing to cooperate; one demand letter will be deemed sufficient though specific content, timing, and number depend on debt type and amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing should allow prompt referral to Department of Justice when needed; written demand does not extend any expired statutory challenge period unless otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of demand letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand letter will inform the debtor of: (1) the basis for the indebtedness and opportunities, if any, to request review within the Commission; (2) applicable standards for assessing interest, penalties, and administrative costs (§§ 1.1940 and 1.1941); (3) the date by which payment is to be made to avoid late charges and enforced collection (normally not more than 30 days from mailing); and (4) the name, address, and phone number of a contact person or office within the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where applicable, demand letters should include the period (normally not more than 15 calendar days) in which to exercise the opportunity to request a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery timing and methods for demand letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will expend reasonable effort to ensure demand letters are mailed or hand-delivered on the same day they are dated; other delivery methods (fax, e-mail) may be used as required by agreement or exigent circumstances and there is no prescribed format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of demand letters/procedures should lead to the earliest practicable determination whether the debt can be resolved administratively or must be referred for litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional content and remedial information in demand letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may include willingness to discuss alternative payment methods; policies regarding use of credit bureaus, debt collection centers, and collection agencies; remedies to enforce payment (interest, administrative costs, garnishment, collection agencies, salary/tax refund/administrative offset, litigation); the requirement to transfer debts delinquent >120 days to Treasury; and, depending on authority, information about the debtor's entitlement to waiver consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, the debtor will be provided a period (normally not more than 15 calendar days) from the date of the demand to request a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission response to debtor communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will respond promptly to communications from the debtor, within 30 days whenever feasible, and will advise debtors who dispute the debt that they must furnish available evidence to support their contentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt responses facilitate administrative resolution prior to referral for litigation or offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation and offset notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to referring a debt for litigation, the Commission will advise each person determined to be liable that litigation may be initiated unless the debt can be collected administratively; this notification follows Executive Order 12988 and may be part of the demand letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government litigation counsel will be advised that the notice has been given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bankruptcy handling in debt collection
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Commission learns a bankruptcy petition has been filed, it may immediately seek legal advice and generally should stop collection activity unless the automatic stay is lifted; usually a proof of claim will be filed and, if a secured creditor, relief from stay may be sought; offset is generally stayed and Commission counsel will determine availability of other remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 11 U.S.C. 106, 362, and 553 for sovereign immunity and stay issues; Commission will determine recoupment and freezing of payments in consultation with counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and exclusions of administrative offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of administrative offset apply as provided in § 1.1901; this section does not apply to certain debts/payments (e.g., Social Security Act debts/payments except as provided, Internal Revenue Code payments, offsets against Federal salaries inconsistent with other regulations, offsets under 31 U.S.C. 3728, statutory or common-law prohibitions, or offsets in judicial proceedings including bankruptcy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debts not subject to offset under 31 U.S.C. 3716 may be collected by other statutory or common-law authorities; see specific exclusions in § 1.1912(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limitation for administrative offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative offset under 31 U.S.C. 3716 to collect a debt may not be conducted more than 10 years after the Government's right to collect the debt first accrued, unless material facts were not known and could not reasonably have been known by responsible officials; this limitation does not apply to debts reduced to judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bankruptcy cases the Commission will seek counsel regarding Bankruptcy Code impacts on offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory centralized administrative offset referral
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission is required to refer past due, legally enforceable nontax debts over 120 days delinquent to the Treasury for collection by centralized administrative offset; debts less than 120 days delinquent may also be referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See FCCS for debt certification requirements; transfer triggers matching by Treasury against Federal payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching/payment offset process and notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and TINs of debtors referred to Treasury will be compared to payee names/TINs on Federal payments; when a match occurs and requirements are met, the payment will be offset and disbursing officials will notify the debtor/payee in writing describing the payment type/amount, offset amount, creditor agency identity, and a contact point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal disbursing officials include Treasury, DoD, USPS, designated disbursing officials; notification is required after offset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due process required before referral for centralized offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Before referring a debt to Treasury for offset, the Commission shall ensure, subject to any agreement/waiver by the debtor, that the debtor has been sent written notice of the debt and the Commission's intent to use administrative offset and has been given: (1) opportunity within 15 days to inspect and copy Commission records related to the debt; (2) opportunity for review within the Commission of the determination of indebtedness (unless waived); and (3) opportunity within 15 days to make a written agreement to repay the debt (otherwise deemed waived).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures may be omitted for recoupments, contractual offsets under Contracts Disputes Act, or where there is insufficient time; when omitted, notice and opportunity for review must be given as soon as practicable and refunds made if owed amounts are later found not owed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification before referral to Treasury
rubrics_metrics.description: Before referring delinquent debts to the Treasury, the Office of Managing Director must certify in a Treasury-acceptable form that the debt(s) is past due and legally enforceable and that the Commission has complied with all due process requirements under 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) and its regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification satisfies certain matching/waiver requirements for Treasury processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from centralized administrative offset and benefit payment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments prohibited by law from offset are exempt from centralized offset. Treasury shall exempt means-tested program payments from centralized offset when requested by the head of the payment certifying agency; benefit payments under the Social Security Act, certain Black Lung and Railroad Retirement benefits may be offset only in accordance with Treasury regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 31 CFR 285.4 and related Treasury rules for exceptions and benefit-specific handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treasury waiver of Computer Matching Act requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3716(f), Treasury may waive Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act requirements for centralized administrative offset upon receipt of a certification from a creditor agency that due process requirements of 31 U.S.C. 3716(a) have been met; this waiver does not apply to offsets under non-centralized or other paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If waiver granted, Data Integrity Board of Treasury oversees matching activities per 31 U.S.C. 3716(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-centralized administrative offset procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-centralized offsets are ad hoc case-by-case offsets the Commission may conduct internally or cooperatively with payment-authorizing agencies when centralized offset is not available/appropriate; debtor due process and certification by the creditor agency are required and payment-authorizing agencies should comply unless offset would be contrary to law or the agency's program interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include OPM offsetting lump-sum payments to Federal employees to satisfy unpaid advances; when collecting multiple debts apply recovered amounts in the best interests of the United States given facts/circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative offset against Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon providing OPM written certification that a debtor has been afforded the procedures in § 1.1912(b)(4), the Commission may request OPM to offset a debtor's anticipated/future benefit payments under the Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund; OPM will flag the account to satisfy timing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process satisfies requirements that offset be initiated prior to expiration of time limitations referenced in § 1.1914(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection in installments: eligibility and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever feasible the Commission shall collect the total amount in one lump sum; if debtor is financially unable, the Commission may accept regular installments (at Commission's sole discretion) after obtaining financial statements and verifying representations and procuring a legally enforceable written agreement specifying terms and acceleration on default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installment terms should, if possible, liquidate the debt in three years or less; obtain sureties or other indicia of creditworthiness where appropriate and follow Federal Credit Reform Act/OMB A-129 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security, denial, and enforcement for installment arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Security for deferred payments will be obtained in appropriate cases; Commission may accept installments even if debtor refuses to execute a written agreement or give security, or may deny extension of credit to any debtor who fails to provide requested records or fails to show ability to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission discretion governs whether to require written agreements or security, and to deny extensions for inadequate documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration of compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may attempt to effect compromise in accordance with standards in 31 CFR part 902 and consider debtor-submitted requests to compromise; such requests should be in writing with full justification addressing 31 CFR 902.2 and include full financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If principal balance exceeds $100,000 (or higher AG-authorized amount) authority to accept compromise rests with DOJ; Commission will evaluate using 31 CFR 902.2 factors and may refer offers to DOJ; DOJ approval is not required if Commission rejects a compromise offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspending or terminating collection action
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension or termination of collection action shall be made in accordance with standards set forth in part 903 of the Federal Claims Collection Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow part 903 criteria for when to suspend or terminate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referrals to Department of Justice and transfer to Treasury
rubrics_metrics.description: Referrals to DOJ shall be made in accordance with part 904 of the FCCS; DCIA requires transfer of delinquent debts to Treasury for collection/cross-servicing per 31 U.S.C. 3711(g), after which the Commission will cease collection activity for the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All non-tax debts delinquent 120 days shall be transferred to Treasury; a debt is past-due if not paid by the date specified in the initial written demand unless other arrangements made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consumer reporting agencies (CRAs): definitions and permissive disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may disclose to a consumer reporting agency, or provide information to Treasury who may disclose to a CRA, information that an individual is responsible for a claim (system information like name, TIN, addresses, telephone numbers, amount, unpaid principal, late period, payment history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission must follow Privacy Act and Federal Claims Collection Act definitions and procedural safeguards before reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements before reporting to consumer reporting agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Before reporting, the Commission will: (1) provide the notice required by 5 U.S.C. 552a(e)(4) that information may be disclosed to a CRA; (2) review the claim to determine it is valid and overdue; (3) make reasonable efforts using debtor-provided info to notify the debtor that payment is overdue, that within not less than 60 days the Commission intends to disclose to a CRA, that information may be disclosed, and (where appropriate) provide explanation and procedures to dispute and seek review; and (4) review Commission records to ensure the individual has not repaid or agreed to repay or has not filed for review under paragraph (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification and a minimum 60-day advance notice are required in typical cases; allow dispute and review processes per rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations to consumer reporting agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall disclose to each CRA any substantial change in the condition/amount of the claim, verify or correct information promptly upon CRA request, and obtain assurances from CRAs that they comply with applicable U.S. laws relating to consumer credit information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accuracy and obtain compliance assurances from CRAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on information disclosed to CRAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Information disclosed to a CRA is limited to information necessary to establish identity (name/address/TIN), the amount, status, and history of the claim, and the agency or program under which the claim arose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit disclosures to minimize privacy impacts consistent with collection objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for CRA referral and commercial debt reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: All accounts in excess of $100 that have been delinquent more than 31 days will normally be referred to a consumer reporting agency. The Commission may also disclose commercial debt accounts (not covered by the Privacy Act) to CRAs under the same provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial debt reporting is subject to Commission rules concerning debt obligations and auction debt agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting for collection services: authority and contractor requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may contract with private collection contractors to recover delinquent debts subject to conditions: Commission retains authority to resolve disputes/compromise/suspend/terminate/referral to litigation; restricts contractors from offering payment incentives that cut their fee unless authorized; requires contractor compliance with Privacy Act (as specified), federal and state debt collection laws (including FDCPA), and accounting for all amounts collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract terms must include Privacy Act compliance, legal debt-collection compliance, and accounting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of government-wide contracts and funding for private collection contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will use government-wide debt collection contracts to obtain services but may also refer debts to private collection contractors via Commission contracts when transfer to Treasury is not required; agencies may fund private collection contractors in accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3718(d) or as otherwise permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow statutory funding mechanisms when engaging private contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts for locating/recovering assets and asset searches
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission may contract for locating and recovering assets (e.g., unclaimed assets) but must first establish procedures acceptable to Treasury before entering contracts to recover assets held by state governments or financial institutions; the Commission may also contract for debtor asset and income search reports and may provide that contractor fees be payable from recovered amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for asset-location/search services may be added to the amount collected and treated as administrative collection costs (see § 1.1940).

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary offset: purpose and scope (individual debt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1.1925 through 1.1939 apply to Commission employees and establish standards to implement 5 U.S.C. 5514 to recover debts from an employee's pay account; these procedures do not apply to debts under the Internal Revenue Code, Social Security Act (with exceptions), tariff laws, or cases where salary offset is explicitly provided for or prohibited by another statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not preclude employee requests for waiver of erroneous payments under other statutory authorities; salary offset procedures should be consistent with FCCS where not specified by 5 U.S.C. 5514.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for initiating salary offset
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 31 CFR 901.3(a)(4) offset may not be initiated more than 10 years after the Government's right to collect the debt first accrued, unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same 10-year limitation principle to salary offset initiation absent an applicable exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements before salary offset deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary offset deductions will not be made unless the Managing Director (or designee) provides the employee at least 30 days before any deduction with written notice stating at minimum: (1) the Commission's determination that a debt is owed including origin, nature, amount; (2) intention to collect by deduction from current disposable pay; (3) frequency and amount of intended deduction (fixed dollar or percentage not to exceed 15% of disposable pay) and intention to continue until paid; (4) explanation of policy concerning interest, penalties, administrative costs; (5) right to inspect and copy government records relating to the debt (or receive copies); and (6) opportunity to establish a voluntary repayment schedule or enter a written agreement in lieu of offset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least 30 days' notice and adequate information so employee can evaluate, inspect records, and pursue voluntary repayment options.
